name: Triple Bypass
start_location: Buchanan Park, Evergreen, CO (Double Bypass starts in Empire, CO). Finish in Avon, CO
date_note: 2027 date not yet announced on triplebypass.org. The ride is usually the second Saturday of July (July 12, 2025; July 11, 2026). Registration for 2026 opened December 3, 2025, and both the Triple and the Double sold out with the waitlist closed.
founded_by: A group of Evergreen-area cyclists who decided to ride from Evergreen to the Vail Valley in one day
registration_note: Registration opens in early December (December 3 for the 2026 ride) on BikeSignup/RunSignup. Both distances sold out for 2026 and the waitlist closed. Entries are non-refundable and cannot be transferred; you can defer, and optional third-party cancellation coverage is offered at checkout. Riders must be 12 or older. Class 1 e-bikes only.

distances.label: Triple Bypass
distances.note: Evergreen to Avon over Juniper, Loveland and Vail passes, 10,800 ft of climbing. Start any time up to 8:00 AM; most leave by 6:30.

distances.label: Double Bypass
distances.note: Empire to Avon over Loveland and Vail passes, 6,500 ft. Mandatory 8:00 AM mass start.

terrain: Paved mountain highways with three long passes and long descents; some sections closed to cars for the ride.
participants: several thousand riders across the Triple and the Double; both distances sold out in 2026
summary: The Triple Bypass is a one-day, 120-mile road ride from Evergreen, Colorado, to Avon in the Vail Valley over Juniper, Loveland and Vail passes, with about 10,800 feet of climbing. It runs on the second Saturday of July and started in 1988 when a group of local cyclists decided to ride Evergreen to Vail in a day. It now draws several thousand riders, sells out, and closes Loveland Pass to cars for the day; an 80-mile Double Bypass starts in Empire.
history: One July day in 1988 a group of Evergreen cyclists decided it would be fun to ride from Evergreen to the Vail Valley. That first ride, over 100 miles with close to 11,000 feet of climbing, became the Triple Bypass. The three passes, Juniper, Loveland and Vail, gave it the name.

The ride became the signature event of Team Evergreen, a local cycling nonprofit, and grew from a few hundred riders to several thousand. It is now produced by Shift Events operating as Team Evergreen. Registration fees feed the club's giving, and riders can also fundraise for one of about a dozen approved charities. The organizers say the event has donated millions to nonprofits over the years.
The 2025 ride was the 37th. Along the way the event added the shorter Double Bypass from Empire and a Blue Sky Hill Climb, and it now closes U.S. 6 over Loveland Pass to car traffic during the ride.
what_to_expect: Riders roll out of Buchanan Park in Evergreen from before dawn; you can start any time but everyone must be on the road by 8:00 AM. The first climb is Juniper Pass on Squaw Pass Road, a long steady grade out of Bergen Park. Then a descent to Idaho Springs, the climb to Loveland Pass on a road closed to cars, Summit County bike paths past Dillon, and Vail Pass before the finish in Avon. Bag drop is at the start and there is a jersey exchange.

Aid stations have cutoff times set by permits and safety. Miss one and your number comes off, with a shuttle to the finish. The Double Bypass field masses at 8:00 AM in Empire and rides the last two passes.

Mornings in Evergreen can start in fog and cloud, as in 2025, before the sun burns through. The fast riders finish in under six hours; most take much of the day. Packet pickup is free and can be done by proxy with a photo of your ID.
weather_note: Around July 11 Evergreen averages a high near 78°F and a low near 54°F, with about a one-in-four chance of rain on a given day. The passes are far higher and colder than the start, and the 2025 ride began in low cloud and dense fog before clearing. Carry a shell and warm layers for the descents.

faq.q: When does registration open and does it sell out?
faq.a: It opens in early December for the following July. Both the Triple and the Double sold out for 2026 and the waitlist closed, so sign up when it opens.

faq.q: Where does it start and finish?
faq.a: The Triple starts at Buchanan Park in Evergreen and finishes in Avon, about 118 road miles away. The Double starts in Empire with an 8:00 AM mass start.

faq.q: How do I get back to Evergreen from Avon?
faq.a: The ride is one way. Arrange a driver or check the organizer's info page for current transport options. Read the road closure notices before planning a pickup.
